digest.headline: Stock futures recovered and Treasury yields climbed toward 5% as global bond markets sold off.

lede.b: Stock futures bounced back today while oil prices dropped down. At the same time, a bond is a loan that investors make to governments or companies, and the yield is the yearly return on that loan. A global bond selloff pushed 10-year US Treasury yields very close to 5%. Treasury yields are the interest rates paid on US government debt. When yields go up, bond prices go down. Meanwhile, Nasdaq made a $100m investment to deepen its partnership with Payward.
lede.i: Stock futures recovered as oil prices slid and investors awaited upcoming inflation data. A broad global bond selloff pushed 10-year Treasury yields near the 5% threshold. Bond prices move inversely to yields, triggering widespread portfolio adjustments. Nasdaq also deepened its partnership with Payward through a $100m investment.
lede.a: Stock futures recovered alongside gold as oil softened ahead of upcoming US price data releases. A global debt selloff drove 10-year Treasury yields toward 5%, reflecting severe sovereign repricing across major jurisdictions. Nasdaq simultaneously expanded its commercial ties with Payward via a $100m strategic capital commitment.

items.b: Stock futures recovered as oil prices fell and 10-year Treasury yields approached 5%.
items.i: Stock futures recovered as oil prices slid, while 10-year Treasury yields approached 5% amid a global bond selloff.

items.a: UK gross domestic product expanded by 0.4% in July, exceeding consensus forecasts as computer programming drove activity.

items.b: The DAX index opened 0.40% higher while Bundesbank President Nagel linked future rate hikes to energy prices.
items.i: The DAX index opened 0.40% higher as Bundesbank President Nagel linked future ECB rate hikes to energy prices.
items.a: The DAX index opened 0.40% higher while Bundesbank President Nagel tied future ECB rate increases to energy developments.

items.a: The Nikkei Stock Average dropped to a one-month low after closing down ¥1,259 amid inflation-linked risk aversion.

thread.b: Several countries faced pressure from rising energy costs and shifting monetary policy expectations. Central bank rate decisions and bond yield changes drove market movements across multiple regions today.
thread.i: Energy price pressures and shifting inflation expectations dominated markets across multiple jurisdictions. Bond yields climbed globally while equities absorbed heavy selling pressure.
thread.a: Sovereign debt repricing and energy price developments drove cross-border equity volatility and currency adjustments. Bond selloffs pushed yields higher in multiple jurisdictions ahead of key macroeconomic releases.

United States of America.label: United States
United States of America.sub: Stock futures recover and Treasury yields rise near 5%

stories.t: Stock Futures and Commodity Reactions Ahead of Inflation Data
stories.b: Stock futures are the prices agreed today for shares to be traded later. They rose as oil prices went down. Gold prices went up toward $4,350. Traders are waiting for the August inflation report to see how fast prices are rising. Inflation means money buys less than it did before.
stories.i: Stock futures recovered as oil prices slid ahead of the August inflation test. Gold prices gained and recovered toward $4,350 as oil softened. Market participants await the upcoming data release to gauge pricing pressures across the economy.
stories.a: Index futures rebounded following a contraction in crude benchmarks, setting up a binary reaction function for the upcoming headline and core prints. Gold appreciated toward $4,350/oz on the softer commodity complex. Real yields and the broader macroeconomic trajectory hinge on whether the upcoming inflation metrics confirm persistent price stickiness.

stories.t: Global Bond Selloff Nears Five Percent Yield Threshold
stories.b: A bond is a loan made by an investor to a government or company. A yield is the yearly return an investor gets on that loan, shown as a percentage. Ten-year Treasury yields are the interest rates paid on 10-year loans to the US government. These yields moved close to 5% during a worldwide bond selloff.
stories.i: A global bond selloff pushed 10-year Treasury yields to the cusp of 5%. Bond prices fall when yields rise, reflecting broader debt market pressures. Investors adjusted portfolios globally as sovereign debt repriced across major jurisdictions.
stories.a: Sovereign debt liquidation drove 10-year US Treasury yields toward the 5% threshold. Duration risk manifested globally as the broader bond selloff accelerated. The implied term premium expanded further as market participants reassessed fiscal supply and central bank balance sheet paths.

stories.t: Nasdaq Expands Payward Partnership With Investment
stories.b: Nasdaq is a big US company that runs a stock exchange where shares are bought and sold. Nasdaq invested $100m to deepen its tie-up with Payward. This move builds on their existing relationship.
stories.i: Nasdaq deepened its partnership with Payward through a $100m investment. The exchange operator expanded its commercial ties with the firm. This strategic commitment extends their operational relationship.
stories.a: Nasdaq increased its exposure to Payward via a $100m capital deployment. The strategic working group participation alongside HKMA, HKEX, and DFSA rounds out the exchange operator's institutional initiatives. The equity stake deepens institutional infrastructure integration between the two entities.

politics.b: Record diesel prices spread the costs of the Iran war across the US economy. Regional financial authorities formed a strategic working group.
politics.i: Record diesel prices propagated Iran war costs throughout the domestic economy. Meanwhile, global regulators including the HKMA, HKEX, DFSA, and Nasdaq Dubai established a strategic working group.
politics.a: Geopolitical shocks from the Iran conflict translated into domestic supply chain pressures via record diesel pricing. Concurrently, cross-border regulatory coordination materialized as the HKMA, HKEX, DFSA, and Nasdaq Dubai formalised a joint strategic working group.

United Kingdom.label: United Kingdom
United Kingdom.sub: UK economy grows as gilts rebound from multi-decade highs

stories.t: UK Economic Growth Exceeds Forecasts in July
stories.b: The UK economy grew by 0.4% in July. This growth came partly from computer programming businesses. The artificial intelligence boom helped lift these technology firms. Official figures showed this expansion for the summer month. Gross domestic product beat earlier market forecasts.
stories.i: Gross domestic product expanded by 0.4% in July, extending the recent growth streak. Computer programming businesses drove part of this activity. Artificial intelligence demand contributed directly to the expansion of technology sectors. The monthly performance beat standard economist forecasts. Sterling remained steady against major currencies following the data release.
stories.a: Monthly GDP expanded by 0.4% in July, outperforming consensus forecasts and extending the current macroeconomic growth streak. Computer programming and related sectors drove the print, with the artificial intelligence boom visibly manifesting in official activity figures. Foreign exchange markets registered little volatility, leaving sterling steady as traders balanced the positive growth surprise against external dollar dynamics.

stories.t: UK Gilts Rebound After Yields Hit Multi-Decade Highs
stories.b: UK government bonds, known as gilts, rose in price slightly on September 11th. This followed a fierce sell-off that had pushed yields to multi-decade highs. A yield is the annual return an investor gets from a bond. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions. The market recovery offered a small pause after heavy selling.
stories.i: UK gilts recovered slightly following a sharp sell-off that drove yields to multi-decade highs. As gilt yields climbed, bond prices fell significantly before this modest stabilization. Investors continued to price in expectations for future monetary policy decisions. The Bank of England maintained its policy stance while navigating aggressive market pricing.
stories.a: Domestic sovereign debt experienced a partial technical retracement after a severe sell-off pushed gilt yields to multi-decade highs. The transmission from aggressive market pricing to terminal rate expectations kept volatility elevated across the curve. The Bank of England remained on hold while market participants adjusted their policy trajectories. This stabilization followed intense selling pressure that had strained duration positions.

stories.t: Bank of England Survey Shows Lower Inflation Expectations
stories.b: Public expectations for future price rises dropped in August. The Bank of England runs this survey with a new provider named Savanta. Price rises are commonly called inflation. Experts noted a catch because the survey provider changed. This change affected the way people answered the questions about future costs.
stories.i: Public inflation expectations declined in the August survey results. The central bank recently changed its survey provider to Savanta, introducing methodological quirks. Analysts noted that the drop in perceived price pressures came with a catch due to this transition. Markets evaluated these survey shifts alongside broader monetary policy settings.
stories.a: Household inflation expectations registered a notable decline in the August Bank of England and Savanta survey. Analysts flagged structural caveats regarding the data given the recent change in survey provider. The downward print in consumer expectations diverged from historical survey metrics. Traders factored these methodological shifts into their broader monetary policy assumptions.

politics.b: The central bank kept interest rates on hold. Political groups debated public spending and past financial choices. Government data showed economic growth continuing through the summer.
politics.i: The Bank of England maintained its policy rate amid aggressive market pricing. Think tanks criticized past institutional spending decisions while contrasting domestic frameworks with international peers. Official data confirmed ongoing economic expansion.
politics.a: Monetary authorities held settings constant against aggressive yield curve pricing. Research organizations published critiques regarding historical institutional expenditure while evaluating alternative international policy models. Macroeconomic releases confirmed persistent output resilience across commercial sectors.

timeline: 11 Aug
Bank of England and Savanta conduct August inflation attitudes survey
11 Sep
July GDP data shows 0.4% economic growth and gilts rebound

Germany.label: Germany
Germany.sub: DAX rebounds as markets watch inflation and energy costs

stories.t: DAX Index Rebounds
stories.b: The DAX index is a stock market index which tracks the forty major German companies trading on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange. The DAX index opened 0.40% higher on Friday. Frankfurt stocks steadied earlier in the morning session.
stories.i: The DAX index opened 0.40% higher on Friday, steadying after extending weekly losses earlier. Traders monitored the session while keeping track of upcoming inflation figures.
stories.a: The DAX posted a rebound on Friday following an extension of weekly losses driven by benchmark index pressure. Price action remained contingent on external macro data releases.

stories.t: Bundesbank President Links Rate Hikes to Energy Prices
stories.b: Bundesbank President Nagel linked further European Central Bank rate hikes to energy prices. The central bank manages the money supply and sets borrowing costs. Further rate increases depend heavily on these energy costs.
stories.i: Bundesbank President Nagel tied future European Central Bank rate hikes directly to energy price developments. The central bank chief warned that the institution may need to enter mildly restrictive territory.
stories.a: Bundesbank President Nagel conditioned subsequent European Central Bank tightening on energy price trajectories. The governing council member emphasised that reaching mildly restrictive policy territory depends entirely on those input costs.

politics.b: Bundesbank President Nagel spoke about monetary policy decisions on Friday. He discussed interest rates in relation to energy costs.
politics.i: Bundesbank President Nagel outlined the conditions for further European Central Bank tightening on Friday. The central bank official focused remarks on energy price dependencies.
politics.a: Bundesbank President Nagel framed future policy calibration around specific energy price thresholds on Friday. The remarks contextualised the governing council's approach to restrictive policy territory.

timeline: Bundesbank President Nagel links European Central Bank rate hikes to energy prices.

Japan.label: Japan
Japan.sub: Japanese markets face rate hike pressure and falling stocks

stories.t: Nikkei Stock Average drops sharply amid global risk aversion
stories.b: The Nikkei Stock Average is a major list of important Japanese company shares. The index hit a one-month low. It closed down by ¥1,259. Middle East tensions and higher crude oil prices caused this drop. Investors sold risky assets like stocks.
stories.i: The Nikkei Stock Average hit a one-month low after closing down ¥1,259. Middle East tensions and a surge in crude oil triggered a broad inflation-linked risk-off move. Equity markets absorbed heavy selling pressure as sentiment deteriorated across the region.
stories.a: The Nikkei Stock Average plummeted to a one-month low, shedding ¥1,259 at the close. Geopolitical friction in the Middle East and a sharp crude oil surge catalyzed a risk-off rotation. Broad equity liquidation reflects heightened macro sensitivity to external supply shocks.

stories.t: Bank of Japan rate hike expectations accelerate volatility
stories.b: The Bank of Japan faces a decision about raising interest rates. Market expectations for a rate hike moved to a quarterly timeline. This shift can unwind carry trades, which are loans in cheap currencies to buy higher-yielding assets. That unwinding causes big swings in stock and bond markets.
stories.i: Market expectations for a Bank of Japan rate hike accelerated to a quarterly timeline. The potential unwinding of carry trades threatens to amplify volatility across equity and bond markets. Further currency gains might also constrain future central bank tightening.
stories.a: Market pricing accelerated Bank of Japan rate hike expectations to a quarterly cadence. The impending unwinding of leveraged carry trades transmits severe volatility shocks into domestic equity and fixed-income structures. Further currency appreciation risks constraining the central bank's normalization path.

politics.b: Japan plans to provide up to 98 billion yen for five additional shipbuilding plans.
politics.i: Japan announced funding of up to 98 billion yen to support 5 additional shipbuilding plans.
politics.a: The Japanese government allocated up to 98 billion yen to back 5 additional shipbuilding initiatives.

timeline: Nikkei Stock Average drops by ¥1,259 to close at a one-month low.

China.label: China
China.sub: Enflame debut, Geely launch, and StarX funding

stories.t: Enflame Shares Jump on Shanghai Stock Exchange
stories.b: Enflame is a company that makes computer chips. Its shares debuted on the Shanghai Stock Exchange, which is a marketplace where people buy and sell ownership pieces of companies. The price jumped by 179%. This happened during a big boom in artificial intelligence, which means computer systems doing smart human-like tasks. Tencent is one of the backers of Enflame.
stories.i: Enflame achieved a stellar debut on the Shanghai Stock Exchange with shares surging 179%. The listing underscores ongoing market enthusiasm for artificial intelligence hardware. Tencent participates as a key backer and partner in the firm.
stories.a: Enflame posted a 179% gain in its initial public offering on the Shanghai Stock Exchange. The pricing reflects sustained capital inflows into domestic artificial intelligence infrastructure. Tencent maintains its position as a primary corporate backer.

stories.t: Geely Launches Galaxy TT and IM Motors Sells SUVs
stories.b: Geely is a vehicle maker in China. It released a new model called the Galaxy TT. This car uses an 800-volt platform and costs at least 129,900 yuan. Meanwhile, IM Motors sold 8,000 units of its refreshed LS6 SUV within 45 minutes.
stories.i: Geely released the Galaxy TT built on an 800-volt platform with a starting price of 129,900 yuan. IM Motors recorded 8,000 orders for its revamped LS6 SUV within a 45-minute window.
stories.a: Geely introduced the Galaxy TT utilizing an 800-volt architecture priced from 129,900 yuan. IM Motors secured 8,000 orders for the revamped LS6 SUV in 45 minutes.

stories.t: StarX Future Secures Funding for Space Constellation
stories.b: StarX Future is a company that works on space technology. It raised hundreds of millions of yuan across two financing rounds. The money will help build a space computing constellation called the Fuyao Project. The project uses 37 orbit-stable advanced process graphics processing units.
stories.i: StarX Future secured hundreds of millions of yuan through two consecutive financing rounds. The capital targets the deployment of 37 orbit-stable advanced process graphics processing units for the Fuyao Project space computing constellation.
stories.a: StarX Future completed two consecutive financing rounds raising hundreds of millions of yuan. The funds support the deployment of 37 orbit-stable advanced process graphics processing units for the Fuyao Project cloud-collaborative space computing constellation.

politics.b: China limited fuel price increases for the third time since the war in Iran began.
politics.i: Regulators limited fuel price increases for the third time following the start of the war in Iran.
politics.a: Authorities capped fuel price increases for the third time since the onset of the conflict in Iran.

timeline: Enflame achieves a 179% return on its debut on the Shanghai Stock Exchange.

India.label: India
India.sub: RBI liquidity operations, government bond auctions, and currency pressures

stories.t: Reserve Bank of India Absorbs Liquidity Through Reverse Repo Auctions
stories.b: The central bank of India manages how much money circulates in the financial system. It held two separate variable rate reverse repo auctions on September 11, 2026. These events let banks store extra cash with the central bank for a set period. Financial institutions offered 3,44,800 crore rupees for a 4-day tenor and 60,449 crore rupees for a 26-day tenor. Both auctions yielded a cut-off rate of 5.24 percent.
stories.i: The Reserve Bank of India absorbed excess banking system liquidity using short-term and medium-term liquidity adjustment facility tools. It allotted 3,44,864 crore rupees in a 4-day variable rate reverse repo auction at a cut-off rate of 5.24 percent. A separate 26-day tenor auction accepted 60,449 crore rupees at the identical rate of 5.24 percent.
stories.a: The central bank sterilized surplus liquidity via dual-tenor variable rate reverse repo operations under the liquidity adjustment facility. Bidding patterns showed 3,44,864 crore rupees accepted across the 4-day window against a 5,00,000 crore rupee notified amount, alongside 60,449 crore rupees taken for the 26-day tenor. Both auctions cleared at a uniform weighted average rate of 5.24 percent.

stories.t: Government Debt Sells at Recent Auctions While Rupee Declines
stories.src: Reserve Bank of India · India markets
stories.b: The Indian government sold debt to investors on September 11, 2026, including 6.20% GS 2029 securities and a new 2056 bond. Meanwhile, the Indian rupee suffered its largest weekly drop in four months. Higher crude oil costs and rising bond yields drove the currency lower for the fourth consecutive day. Stock indexes also reacted as the Nifty Metal index fell 3 percent due to regional tensions in West Asia.
stories.i: The Reserve Bank of India published auction results for government stock maturing in 2029, 2033, and 2056, accepting 4,505.529 crore rupees for the partial 2029 tranche. Simultaneously, the Indian rupee posted its sharpest weekly decline in four months. Rising crude oil prices and increasing yields pressured the currency across four consecutive sessions.
stories.a: The debt management office issued paper across the 2029, 2033, and 2056 tenors, accepting 4,505.529 crore rupees for the partial 6.20% 2029 GS issue at an implicit yield of 6.4031 percent. Concurrently, macroeconomic headwinds drove the rupee to its steepest weekly contraction in four months. Crude oil appreciation and upward yield trajectories spurred foreign exchange outflows over four consecutive trading sessions.

politics.b: The central bank extended administrative directions for The Gujarat Rajya Karmachari Co-op. Bank Ltd until September 11, 2026.
politics.i: The Reserve Bank of India extended regulatory directions under Section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, for The Gujarat Rajya Karmachari Co-op. Bank Ltd until September 11, 2026.
politics.a: Regulatory oversight persisted for The Gujarat Rajya Karmachari Co-op. Bank Ltd via an extension of directions under Section 35A read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, running until the close of business on September 11, 2026.

timeline: The Reserve Bank of India issued directions to The Gujarat Rajya Karmachari Co-op. Bank Ltd.
The Reserve Bank of India conducted variable rate reverse repo auctions and government stock sales.

Brazil.label: Brazil
Brazil.sub: Petrobras plans fuel price adjustments and secures deals

stories.t: Petrobras Weighs Fuel Price Adjustments
stories.b: Petrobras wants to raise diesel prices. It is waiting for government steps to protect consumers first. Meanwhile, the company cancelled a gasoline hike. The gasoline price fell by R$0.19 following tax cuts.
stories.i: Petrobras seeks to implement a diesel price increase while awaiting government measures to protect consumers. The company simultaneously cancelled a planned gasoline hike, leaving the price down by R$0.19 after tax cuts.
stories.a: Petrobras targets a diesel price adjustment conditional on fiscal or regulatory shielding mechanisms from the state. Management cancelled the separate gasoline hike, allowing prices to decline by R$0.19 following structural tax reductions.

stories.t: Braskem Extends Supply Deal With Petrobras
stories.b: Braskem extended its natural gas supply agreement with Petrobras. The deal runs through 2029. Petrobras also drew $1.4bn in bids for a subsea tender.
stories.i: Braskem prolonged its natural gas supply agreement with Petrobras through 2029. Petrobras separately secured $1.4bn in bids for a subsea tender.
stories.a: Braskem extended its natural gas procurement contract with Petrobras through 2029, locking in feedstock visibility. Petrobras concurrently drew $1.4bn in bids for its subsea tender, reflecting robust offshore capital expenditure pipelines.

politics.b: The government is looking at steps to protect consumers from diesel price changes. Petrobras has to wait for these official measures.
politics.i: State involvement shapes fuel pricing as Petrobras awaits government measures to shield consumers before raising diesel costs.
politics.a: State intervention constrains pricing autonomy as Petrobras conditions its diesel tariff hike on explicit government consumer-shielding policies.

Saudi Arabia.label: Saudi Arabia
Saudi Arabia.sub: Saudi oil output drops and Aramco considers asset sales

stories.t: Saudi Oil Production Falls to Lowest Level Since 1990
stories.b: Saudi Arabia produced less oil in August than at any time since 1990. Oil is a black liquid pumped from the ground and turned into petrol and other fuels. The drop happened during the conflict between the United States and Iran. Total production across the wider OPEC group fell by 640,000 barrels per day in August.
stories.i: Saudi crude output dropped to its lowest level since 1990 following fallout from the US-Iran war. Total OPEC production fell by 640,000 barrels per day over the month of August. Meanwhile, Asian buyers asked Saudi Aramco to alter its crude pricing benchmarks to Brent.
stories.a: Saudi production slumped to 1990 lows amid regional conflict spillovers linked to the US-Iran war, compounding an OPEC-wide output contraction of 640,000 barrels per day in August. Concurrently, Asian refiners pressed Saudi Aramco to price crude against Brent rather than traditional regional markers, reflecting shifting buyer leverage.

stories.t: Public Investment Fund Considers Gaming Merger and Aramco Evaluates Arlanxeo Sale
stories.b: Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund is looking at merging Electronic Arts with Savvy Games Group. A fund is a large pool of money collected from investors to buy assets. At the same time, Saudi Aramco is thinking about selling its Arlanxeo business. Aramco is the massive state-owned oil company of Saudi Arabia.
stories.i: Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund weighed a merger between Electronic Arts and Savvy Games Group. Simultaneously, Saudi Aramco considered a sale of its subsidiary Arlanxeo. These portfolio adjustments occur as broader venture capital deals continue involving Aramco Ventures.
stories.a: The Public Investment Fund evaluated a consolidation transaction combining Electronic Arts with Savvy Games Group. Parallel asset rationalisation saw Saudi Aramco explore the divestment of Arlanxeo. These corporate actions sit alongside ongoing venture capital deployment via Aramco Ventures.

politics.b: Government officials and state-backed funds in Saudi Arabia direct large investments into global gaming and energy businesses. State leaders manage oil production alongside international partners in OPEC. Geopolitical tensions involving foreign nations directly impact local industrial output.
politics.i: Saudi state entities direct capital allocation through major vehicles like the Public Investment Fund and Aramco. Production quotas are managed in coordination with OPEC member states. Foreign policy friction alters domestic output metrics.
politics.a: State-directed capital deployment relies on coordinated output management within OPEC frameworks alongside aggressive sovereign wealth acquisitions. Geopolitical exposure to external conflicts directly dictates domestic extraction limits and asset strategies.

timeline: Saudi oil output drops to its lowest level since 1990.
OPEC total output falls by 640,000 barrels per day in August.

Nigeria.label: Nigeria
Nigeria.sub: Dangote share offer, Naira movements and oil output

stories.t: Dangote Refinery Plans September Share Offer
stories.b: Dangote Refinery will open a share offer on 14 September. Investors can buy shares for 525 naira each. A share is a tiny piece of a company. Buying shares means you own part of the business.
stories.i: Dangote Refinery opens a 525 naira share offer on 14 September. Local investors continue to dominate the Nigerian stock market. This comes despite the country's return to the FTSE frontier index.
stories.a: Dangote Refinery initiates a 525 naira equity offering on 14 September. Domestic participants retain market dominance despite the venue's readmission to the FTSE frontier index.

stories.t: Naira Strengthens Against Major Currencies
stories.b: The Nigerian currency is called the naira. The naira got stronger against the dollar and the euro on 11 September. Better foreign exchange liquidity caused this. Liquidity means having enough money available to trade easily.
stories.i: The naira strengthened to N1,548/€ against the euro on 11 September. The currency also made gains against the dollar at the official foreign exchange market. Improved FX liquidity drove these changes.
stories.a: The naira appreciated to N1,548/€ against the euro on 11 September alongside marginal gains against the greenback at the official fix. Enhanced FX liquidity underpinned the currency's upward movement across multiple pairs.

stories.t: Nigerian Oil Output Falls as OPEC Increases Supply
stories.b: Nigeria produced less oil on 11 September. Other members of OPEC increased their own oil production at the same time. OPEC is a group of countries that work together to sell oil.
stories.i: Nigeria's oil output dipped again on 11 September. Other OPEC members ramped up production simultaneously. This reduction occurred while some Nigerian firms reclaimed pre-devaluation profit levels in dollar terms.
stories.a: Nigeria's petroleum output contracted further on 11 September as broader OPEC constituents accelerated extraction volumes. Concurrently, domestic corporates reclaimed 2023 pre-devaluation earnings parity in hard currency terms.

politics.b: Governor Soludo supported Tinubu's re-election on 11 September. Soludo predicted a stronger economy in four years. Obi also backed Tinubu's naira float policy on the same day.
politics.i: Governor Soludo backed Tinubu's re-election on 11 September, predicting a stronger Nigerian economy within four years. Obi backed Tinubu's naira float policy on the same date.
politics.a: Governor Soludo endorsed Tinubu's re-election bid on 11 September, forecasting macroeconomic strengthening over a four-year horizon. Obi concurrently voiced support for Tinubu's naira float policy.

timeline: The naira strengthened against the dollar, pound, and euro at the official market.
Nigeria's oil output dipped as OPEC members ramped up production.
Dangote Refinery opens its 525 naira share offer.

Australia.label: Australia
Australia.sub: Australian shares fall on bond yields, oil and copper

stories.t: Australian Shares Decline as Bond Yields and Oil Pressure Markets
stories.b: Australian shares dropped as bond yields, which measure the return on government debt, climbed higher alongside oil prices. Investors worried about recessions and interest rate pressures. Major mining companies like BHP and Rio Tinto fell on the ASX after copper prices dropped. Dataworks Group placed its stock in a trading halt.
stories.i: Australian shares fell as soaring bond yields and rising oil prices added pressure to equity markets. Mining giants BHP and Rio Tinto declined on the ASX alongside a drop in copper prices. Dataworks Group initiated a trading halt while Indiana Resources completed a heritage survey at Ealbara.
stories.a: Australian equities retreated as sovereign bond yields extended their rise and commodity prices weakened. BHP and Rio Tinto faced selling pressure on the ASX following a decline in copper futures. Dataworks Group requested a trading halt while Indiana Resources progressed exploration plans at Ealbara.

stories.t: Australian Dollar Holds Steady Against Yen on RBA Signals
stories.b: The Australian dollar held steady against the Japanese yen. Hawkish signals from the Reserve Bank of Australia helped offset strength in the yen. Australia faces an economic outlook featuring slow growth, sticky inflation, and higher interest rates.
stories.i: The Australian dollar steadied against the Japanese yen as hawkish signals from the Reserve Bank of Australia offset carry trade dynamics and currency strength. The broader Australian economy faced headwinds from slow growth, sticky inflation, and elevated interest rates through 2026.
stories.a: The Australian dollar maintained its level versus the Japanese yen as hawkish Reserve Bank of Australia communication countered currency strength. The domestic macroeconomic backdrop featured sluggish GDP growth, persistent inflation, and restrictive interest rates.

politics.b: Economic reports outlined slower growth and higher rates across Australia.
politics.i: Market commentators highlighted persistent inflation and elevated rates shaping the Australian economy.
politics.a: Analyses pointed to structural growth constraints and restrictive monetary policy settings across Australia.

timeline: ASX shares fall as bond yields and oil prices climb.
BHP and Rio Tinto drop on the ASX following copper price declines.
Australian dollar steadies against the Japanese yen amid RBA signals.
